command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp
cd /tmp

# spawn runs task commands under bash -e; `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it (spawn#707).
# PATH export IS needed: aarchbio images have their PATH dropped by the task shell.

echo "== staged bytes must match their pin =="
sha256sum -c pins.sha256 || { echo "FAIL: dataset.tar does not match its pin"; exit 1; }
tar -xf dataset.tar
TAG=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="dataset_tag"{print $2}' expected.tsv)
NSEQ=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="n_sequences"{print $2}' expected.tsv)

echo "== the dataset must still self-report the staged tag =="
# Checked with grep rather than an interpreter. This runs in a single-tool bioconda image
# built around a Rust binary, which ships no interpreter at all -- and the first version hid
# that behind a stderr redirect, so "command not found" surfaced as an empty tag and the
# failure message blamed the dataset, which was perfect. A diagnostic must never be able to
# obscure its own cause. Asserting the staged tag appears in pathogen.json IS the claim.
printf 'dataset_tag_expected\t%s\n' "$TAG"
if grep -q "\"$TAG\"" dataset/pathogen.json; then
  printf 'dataset_tag_reported\t%s\n' "$TAG"
else
  echo "FAIL: pathogen.json does not declare tag $TAG"
  grep -o '"tag"[^,]*' dataset/pathogen.json | head -3
  exit 1
fi

nextclade --version 2>&1 | head -1

echo "== self-identity: the reference aligned to its own dataset =="
# The dataset's reference IS the coordinate system, so running it as a query must find zero
# differences. Algorithmic, exact, and independent of any lineage question.
nextclade run --input-dataset dataset --output-tsv ref.tsv --output-all ref_out \
  dataset/reference.fasta > nc_ref.log 2>&1
test "$?" = "0" || { tail -20 nc_ref.log; echo "FAIL: nextclade on the reference failed"; exit 1; }
awk -F'\t' 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++)h[$i]=i; next}
  { printf "ref_totalSubstitutions\t%s\n", $(h["totalSubstitutions"])
    printf "ref_totalDeletions\t%s\n",     $(h["totalDeletions"])
    printf "ref_totalInsertions\t%s\n",    $(h["totalInsertions"])
    printf "ref_totalMissing\t%s\n",       $(h["totalMissing"]) }' ref.tsv | tee refid.tsv
S=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="ref_totalSubstitutions"{print $2}' refid.tsv)
D=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="ref_totalDeletions"{print $2}' refid.tsv)
I=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="ref_totalInsertions"{print $2}' refid.tsv)
test "${S:-x}" = "0" -a "${D:-x}" = "0" -a "${I:-x}" = "0" || {
  echo "FAIL: the reference differs from itself (subs $S, del $D, ins $I)"; exit 1; }
printf 'identity_reference\treference vs its own dataset: 0 substitutions, 0 indels\n'

echo "== call the 165 example sequences =="
nextclade run --input-dataset dataset --output-tsv nextclade.tsv \
  dataset/sequences.fasta > nc.log 2>&1
test "$?" = "0" || { tail -25 nc.log; echo "FAIL: nextclade run failed"; exit 1; }
ROWS=$(( $(wc -l < nextclade.tsv) - 1 ))
printf 'nextclade_rows\t%s\n' "$ROWS"
test "$ROWS" = "$NSEQ" || { echo "FAIL: $ROWS rows for $NSEQ sequences"; exit 1; }

# Carry forward exactly what the comparison needs: name and Pango call.
awk -F'\t' 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++)h[$i]=i
    if(!("seqName" in h)){print "FAIL: no seqName column" > "/dev/stderr"; exit 2}
    pc = ("Nextclade_pango" in h) ? h["Nextclade_pango"] : 0
    if(pc==0){print "FAIL: no Nextclade_pango column" > "/dev/stderr"; exit 2}
    print "seqName\tnextclade_pango\tclade"; next}
  { print $(h["seqName"]) "\t" $(pc) "\t" $(h["clade"]) }' nextclade.tsv > nc_calls.tsv
test "$?" = "0" || { echo "FAIL: could not extract Nextclade pango calls"; exit 1; }
wc -l < nc_calls.tsv | awk '{print "nc_calls_rows\t"$1-1}'
head -3 nc_calls.tsv | sed 's/^/  /'
awk -F'\t' 'NR>1 && $2!="" {n++} END{printf "nextclade_pango_assigned\t%d\n", n+0}' nc_calls.tsv

{ printf 'observable\tvalue\n'; cat refid.tsv
  printf 'nextclade_rows\t%s\n' "$ROWS"; } > nc_score.tsv
echo "NEXTCLADE OK"
